[09/12, 9:21 am] Meta AI: Yes, there is a phenomenon known as "hypoglycemia hyperawareness" or "hypoglycemia anxiety," although it is not as widely discussed or researched as hypoglycemia unawareness.

Hypoglycemia hyperawareness refers to an increased sensitivity and awareness of bodily sensations that may be misinterpreted as hypoglycemia, even when blood glucose levels are within a normal range. This can lead to anxiety, fear, and stress related to hypoglycemia.

Studies suggest that hypoglycemia hyperawareness can be more common in individuals with diabetes who have experienced previous episodes of hypoglycemia, particularly if they were severe or traumatic. It can also be seen in individuals with anxiety disorders or those who are prone to catastrophic thinking.

The literature suggests that hypoglycemia hyperawareness can be addressed through education, cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and relaxation techniques. It's essential to work with a healthcare provider to develop strategies to manage hypoglycemia anxiety and improve overall quality of life.

References:

- Cryer, P. E. (2013). Hypoglycemia in Diabetes. Diabetes, 62(12), 4083–4089.
- McAulay, V., & Frier, B. M. (2001). Hypoglycemia: A Clinical Approach. Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism, 86(10), 4739–4746.
- Wild, D., & von Maltzahn, R. (2008). Hypoglycemia and Anxiety in People with Diabetes. Journal of Diabetes and its Complications, 22(3), 175–184.
